status: proposal (claude-a/progression, 25 Oct); every number is a placeholder until play-tests and Claude L's harness

builds_on.abilities: game/data/abilities/<id>.json (Codex C60, PR #261, branch codex/godot-ability-kits): the base kit and the powered form are canonical and unchanged here
builds_on.game_design: docs/vision/game-design.md (PR #223): level 1 to 30 shared, gear level and the forge, Glint, scrap and region materials; its perk card is replaced by the skill tree

levels.skill_points: one point at every level from 2 to 30 (29 in all); Glint never buys points
levels.late_joiner: arrives at the shared level with all its points unspent, and a 'choose for me' button that follows the folk's first branch
levels.replaces: game-design.md section 6's perk card of three: its ideas are folded into each folk's tree as minor nodes
levels.inputs: no new buttons: every technique binds to primary, secondary, block, special, dodge, a timing window or a passive condition. None uses a hold on primary (Codex's primary repeats while held)

skill_tree.shape: three branches per folk, each matching part of its kit; five nodes a branch, fifteen in all
skill_tree.levels_note: levels[i] is the level a node unlocks in branch i (branch 1, 2, 3); a node also needs the node before it in its branch
skill_tree.budget: the whole tree costs 33 points and a folk earns 29 by level 30, so a finished folk has everything except one keystone: the build choice is which keystone to leave out, and the order you take nodes in
skill_tree.modifiers: every node is a modifier layered over the canonical kit at run time; game/data/abilities/*.json is never edited

respec.note: refunds every point; never in a fight, siege or dungeon

buys: outfits and accessories at Moss's stall
forge work (weapon tiers, fittings set and moved, gear level)
shops and map services (fast travel extras, the lookout's markers, seeds, tonics)

rules: Each folk keeps one signature weapon, the item its kit is built on (Matt, 25 Oct). Tiers change its drawing and add one small handling change each.
Tiers are level milestones: a tier opens at its level, then Hale forges it cheaply, per folk (Matt, 25 Oct).
No tier multiplies damage. Power comes from gear level and the forge (game-design.md 5.6 and appendix B).
Loot is fittings: weapon drops are fittings with game-design's rarity and affixes, set into the signature weapon's sockets at the forge (moved freely, a small Glint fee). Sockets grow with the tier.
Tier sizes are relative to the tier-1 drawing (Bramble's bow is being redrawn larger in cast v2).
A tier keeps the weapon's grip and release anchors within 1 px; a longer tier records its own anchors in the manifest.
A folk who joins late arrives at the highest tier any folk has reached, except Starfall, which is always a forge step.
weapon_tiers.starshard: a fist-sized splinter of moon; guaranteed on the first defeat of every boss from act 3 on and from the deep shards after the story; Moss's stall sells them at a fixed price after the story. Never random-priced, never timed
weapon_tiers.smith: Hale, at the forge (game/core/village.gd restore id 'forge'); 'Show me' previews the next tier on the folk before paying

cosmetics.rule: Outfits are looks only. Accessories are looks only, except each folk's trinket, which carries one small perk marked 'proposal'. Only the active folk's trinket counts, so perks never stack.

slots.outfit: the body's cloth and colours; one at a time; 'home' is the drawn look
slots.head: a hat or headpiece; for Ashe, Brine and Rook it dresses the helmet instead (a hat cannot coexist with the helmet they wear)
slots.back: cloak, cape or what rides on the back; never hides tagged back gear (quiver, pack, slung rifle, loader frame)
slots.trinket: a small belt or chest charm, 2 to 4 px

sources.story: a quest's end: the folk's own quest (game-design 8.3) or a named main or village quest. Event quest:<id>:done; quest ids are Claude K's and are placeholders here
sources.arena: a first rank in a ring (game-design 9). Event arena:<ring>:<bronze|silver|gold>. Never Star (Hard only)
sources.village: a building restored to a tier (game-design 7.3). Event restore:<building>:<tier>
sources.bond: any familiar reaching a bond level (game-design 4.1). Event bond:any:<level>
sources.drop: a rare drop from camp chests and elites in one region (looter-lite). Event drop:<region>
sources.glint: bought at Moss's stall at a fixed price once the stall tier stocks it. Event buy:stall:<item>

drop_rules.bad_luck_counter: guaranteed by the 12th camp chest in that region
drop_rules.drops_for_folk_not_yet_met: kept in the wardrobe, shown when they join

cosmetics.ramps: names in item 'ramps' and tier 'materials' are descriptive; '(new)' marks a ramp to add to castwork palette.py with four tones (deep, shadow, base, light, optional shine); others name the material already on that part

save.status: proposal for the save owner; nothing here changes game/core/save_game.gd

fields.folk.<id>.fittings: [fitting ids or null], one per socket
fields.folk.<id>.look: {outfit, head, back, neck, trinket}: item ids or null
fields.folk.<id>.nodes: [node ids] taken in the tree; unspent points = (level - 1) - spent
